one_liner: Archived Python deep learning framework whose hand-assembled Maxwell GPU convolution kernels beat cuDNN R4 by 1.2-2x on 2016 ConvNet benchmarks.
what_it_does: neon is Intel Nervana's Python training framework (layers, optimizers, model zoo) with swappable backends: a GPU backend (NervanaGPU, driven through PyCUDA), an MKL CPU backend and a plain NumPy CPU backend. The speed claim is about its GPU convolution, GEMM and pooling kernels, which you reach through neon models or the lower-level NervanaGPU / layer_gpu ConvLayer objects in Python. There is no documented C or C++ API for the kernels, so it is not a drop-in replacement for cuDNN calls.
how_it_is_fast: The kernels are written directly in NVIDIA SASS (shader assembly) and assembled with maxas, Scott Gray's Maxwell assembler, so register allocation, instruction scheduling and control codes are hand-tuned rather than left to nvcc. For 3x3 stride-1 convolutions the backend uses Winograd minimal filtering, F(2x2,3x3) and F(4x4,3x3) variants for fprop, bprop and weight update, which cuts the multiplies per output. fp16 storage halves memory traffic, and the convnet-benchmarks script passes hand-picked per-layer tile shapes (grid_P, grid_Q, update_size) to each ConvLayer.
when_to_use: Reproducing or studying the 2016 convnet-benchmarks results on Maxwell (GTX 9xx, Titan X) or Pascal GPUs, where the SASS kernels were tuned.
Learning hand-written SASS GEMM and Winograd convolution techniques: the .sass sources, maxas and the Python kernel wrappers are Apache-2.0 (maxas is MIT).
Legacy neon models that already run on a Maxwell/Pascal box with CUDA 7.x-8.0 and Python 2.7/3 environments of that era.
when_not_to_use: Any new project: the repository was archived on 2023-01-03 with an Intel discontinuation notice, and the last release is v2.6.0 (January 2018).

Volta, Turing, Ampere, Hopper or later GPUs: maxas is described as an 'Assembler for NVIDIA Maxwell architecture' and nothing in the repo documents support beyond Maxwell/Pascal; pre-Maxwell GPUs fall back to slower CUDA C kernels.
C++ codebases: the kernels are driven from Python through PyCUDA, with no supported native API.
Comparisons against current cuDNN: the measured baseline is cuDNN R4, and cuDNN R4 still won AlexNet (71 vs 78 ms fp16, 81 vs 87 ms fp32).
Modern Python stacks: requirements pin 2016-2018 packages (numpy 1.13.1, Pillow 3.3.2, PyYAML 4.2b1, pycuda >= 2015.1, scikit-cuda 0.5.1).

integration.form: module (Python package nervananeon; SASS kernels JIT-assembled into cubins on first use)
integration.dependencies: PyCUDA, scikit-cuda, numpy, h5py, aeon data loader (separate install), CUDA toolkit with ptxas on PATH, Perl for maxas; MKLML for the CPU backend
integration.min_toolchain: Python 2.7 or 3 (setup.py classifiers), CUDA 7.0-8.0 era toolkit (Makefile searches cuda-8.0, cuda-7.5, cuda-7.0)
integration.platforms: Linux and macOS; NVIDIA compute capability 5.0+ for SASS kernels (5.2+ for fp16), 3.0+ via CUDA C fallback kernels; x86 CPUs via MKL
integration.thread_safety: not documented (the GPU backend owns a PyCUDA context and a cuBLAS handle created at backend init)

gotchas: Kernels are assembled at runtime by running ptxas and maxas.pl and cached under ~/.cache/neon/kernels; issue #416 shows ptxas failing with a floating-point exception for sm_61 under CUDA 9.0, closed without a documented fix.
Open issue #461 (2019, GTX 1050 Mobile, CUDA 10.0) reports 90.2% misclassification on the MNIST MLP example with the GPU backend while other backends train normally; it never got a reply.

The suite's fp16/fp32 rows were produced with the separate nervanagpu package (convnew branch) and Nervana's limited-release beta kernels; neon ships a descendant script, neon/backends/convnet-benchmarks.py, that runs the same nets through neon's own NervanaGPU backend (fp16 and AlexNet/BN variants by default).
The convnet-benchmarks script hard-codes per-layer tile parameters (grid_P, grid_Q, update_size) tuned for the benchmarked shapes, so other layer shapes may not see the same speedup.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: None of the catalogued siblings is a GPU convolution library: NNPACK is the CPU Winograd/FFT convolution counterpart, and LIBXSMM, FeatherCNN and MNN target CPUs. Pick neon only to study or reuse its SASS Winograd/GEMM kernels on Maxwell/Pascal; for current NVIDIA GPUs the cuDNN baseline itself has since added Winograd and is the practical choice.
verified_claims_summary: soumith/convnet-benchmarks (independent; i7-5930K + Titan X, Ubuntu 14.04, full forward+backward, averaged over 10 runs) lists Nervana-neon beside cuDNN R4 via Torch: OxfordNet model A 320 vs 529 ms fp32 and 254 vs 471 ms fp16, GoogleNet V1 270 vs 470 ms fp32 and 230 vs 462 ms fp16, Overfeat 211 vs 268 ms fp32 and 176 vs 242 ms fp16, while cuDNN R4 wins AlexNet. No compiler, driver or CUDA versions are stated, and the kernels benchmarked were the nervanagpu beta release rather than a tagged neon build.
status_note: Abandoned: archived 2023-01-03, last commit 2019-05-22, Intel accepts no patches; Apache-2.0, so the SASS kernels and Winograd wrappers can be copied for study, but they will not run unchanged on GPUs newer than Pascal according to anything the repo documents.
